Intellectual disability and Hirschsprung disease define the syndrome; congenital heart abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Incontinence alone does not establish urinary tract damage.
Benign neoplasm arising from the duodenal wall.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder; profound developmental delay and seizures in 2/2, with brain degeneration. Hepatic deposits alone do not establish liver dysfunction.
Toxic basal ganglia injury defines manganism; visual dysfunction is reported in 30-79%. Inhalational exposure alone does not establish pulmonary injury.
Malignant tumor arising in the orbit; skeletal muscle differentiation does not establish a separate musculoskeletal site.
Umbrella of inherited pyrimidine metabolism disorders; neurologic, hematologic and muscular damage vary substantially among subtypes.
Distal, ocular and pharyngeal myopathy define disease; pharynx maps to pulmonary. Brain atrophy reported in 3/3; cardiac findings from small reports omitted under the four-axis cap.
Infectious abscess directly occupies and damages liver tissue.
CNS hypomyelination defines disease; dental abnormalities and myopia each occur in 3/8 patients (~38%), supporting oral and ocular involvement.
Benign neoplasm of the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the available axes.
Oral, digital and characteristic brain malformations define this ciliopathy; hydronephrosis reported in 1/1 patient supports renal involvement, with limited frequency evidence.
Hereditary tremor and normal pressure hydrocephalus are neurologic disorders; associated gait abnormalities do not establish another damaged organ.
Brain malformations, axon guidance defects and congenital extraocular muscle fibrosis define the spectrum; endocrine abnormalities and contractures are variable.
Neoplasm of the common bile duct; extrahepatic bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Apolipoprotein A-I deficiency is an inherited HDL metabolism disorder; atherosclerosis is a separate disease, and corneal deposits need not impair vision.
Multiple peripheral and spinal nerve sheath tumors define disease. Hearing loss, cataracts and skeletal changes are occasional; skin damage is not established across the group.
Parasitic echinococcal infection with proliferating hepatic hydatid cysts; common direct damage to another organ is not established.
Inherited globin synthesis disorder causing microcytic anemia; severe-form skeletal changes and treatment-related iron overload are not general features.
Epilepsy with developmental encephalopathy or progressive neurologic deterioration; immune mechanisms do not apply across this umbrella.
Inherited platelet deficiency and dysfunction define disease; hematologic malignancy is a predisposition rather than an additional affected organ.
CoQ10 deficiency with encephaloneuropathy and deafness; aortic/mitral regurgitation in 2/2 supports cardiac involvement. Optic atrophy (2/2) omitted under four-axis cap.
Lacrimal, salivary/dental and ear abnormalities define syndrome; digital skeletal malformations are major diagnostic features and occur in 30-79%.
Congenital skeletal muscle weakness and atrophy; ophthalmoplegia in 2/5 (~40%) and recurrent ptosis support ocular involvement. Isolated hydrocephalus does not establish common CNS disease.
Axonal and demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; denervation muscle damage with limb weakness in ~60-67% and prominent fixed foot deformity supports musculoskeletal involvement.
